about: Round 4's routing table, pre-registered data. Decided by routing.py only, from harness-side records only, never from the agent's text. Route, phase, turn-end and batch-state strings are graders/labels4.py's and are checked against it on load. A row matches when the take is in its phase, every all_of condition holds, at least one any_of condition holds (when any_of is given), and no none_of condition holds. The winning rows are the matched rows at the highest precedence level; matched rows at that level that name different routes are a tie and are refused, as is an input that matches no row. Rows never read a text-derived count (the events record): those are annotations, below.
plan_source: Round 4 plan, 'What round 4 measures' > 'Outcomes' > routing table and its precedence paragraph; CP1 task 'CREATE .../routing.py'.
precedence_source: Plan: 'pause, then aborted, then harness-error, then graded'. Lane w1b decision: rehearsal shares harness-error's level (both are harness faults, split only by phase), so a double match between them is refused, never picked.

claude-code.source: glitch-f3's ruling (in-plan, 6 Oct 2026, on lane w1b's open question whether a subscription usage-limit refusal carries a structured field; recorded as glitch-f3's, not the owner's): "Keep both: structured (status 429, type rate_limit_error) OR round 3's four text markers ('rate limit', 'usage limit', 'weekly limit', '429'), word-bounded and case-insensitive, matched on the harness-side error text only, never on the agent's own output. Make the small schema change so the API-error record carries that text." status and type match by exact membership. text is the API-error record's harness-side error text (what Claude Code or the API reported as the error, never the agent's reply), and it matches when it carries a text marker by round 3's bounded search (routing.rate_limit_text_marker): each marker word-bounded and case-insensitive. Round 3's origin: the text markers are round 3's RATE_LIMIT_MARKERS, in order, from evals/gap-study-3/drive.py:149 at e2979b3143081824aadea73523ec41af30c1ddb1 (which that line names as prereg.json driver_constants.rate_limit_markers; prereg.json itself was not read by lane w1b for this), matched there by matched_marker and looks_rate_limited (drive.py:906-923; the search at 912-919); round 3 left 'resets' out (its review 13, F6). tests/test_routing.py TestRound3Sources re-derives the tuple with ast from drive.py:149 and runs round 3's own matched_marker against routing's match. Plan: 'a pre-registered rate-limit marker in the API-error record'. Keys are API-error record fields (routing.py checks this). Keyed by harness (lane w4h-w1b-next-touch, w1b's next-touch item 1; CP2-requirements, the spend-cap section: the rate-limit markers and the reset wait come from a table keyed by the adapter's harness, AgentAdapter.name, claude-code keeping round 3's values exactly; a harness-keyed table in routing.json beyond interface 8's three seam modules, approved by glitch-f3's C3 and D8 rulings, W4BR-w4h-6); the rate-limit row reads the take's own harness's entry (records pin.harness), and a harness with no entry is refused, never defaulted. reset_wait: null, round 3's: evals/gap-study-3/drive.py:140-160 at e2979b3143081824aadea73523ec41af30c1ddb1 states no reset wait (its constants there are PERMISSION_MODE, WALK_CAP, FINALIZE_WAIT_S = 180, stage 00's finalize wait at line 146 and no reset wait, and RATE_LIMIT_MARKERS at 149); named for CP2's wait_reset, which reads the vendor's own reset signal per harness.

spend_cap_refusal.source: A vendor spend cap is not a rate limit (glitch-f3, Tue 6 Oct 2026 22:42 EDT, CP2-requirements, the spend-cap section; w1b's next-touch item 1), as a closed refusal rule shaped like pin_refusal (glitch-f3's ruling 4, Thu 8 Oct 2026 17:25 EDT; recorded as glitch-f3's, not the owner's): 'The spend-cap row is a closed refusal rule, shaped like pin_refusal. It raises RoutingRefused, so batch records the take blocked, and it ranks above pause.' In every phase (when any) and outranked by nothing (W4BR-w4h-7): an API error of the take whose status, type or text carries a spend-cap marker of the take's own harness (spend_cap_markers, read by the take's pin.harness; text by round 3's bounded search, word-bounded and case-insensitive; the harness-side error fields only, never the agent's reply) is refused for a human ruling, whatever else matches, so a spend-cap 429 never reaches the rate-limit row: it never re-runs and never waits for a usage window. No route is added to labels4.ROUTES. routing.py checks the rule: its keys, its phase, an empty outranked_by, and conditions that read only the API-error fields with in_spend_cap_markers; and that no spend-cap marker of a harness is also one of its rate-limit markers.

transcript-unreadable.ruling: glitch-b5's ruling on review r8's finding 1, 16 Oct 2026, under Javier's delegation: str.splitlines() also splits on U+2028, U+2029, \x85 and other separators, which Claude Code's JSON writer leaves raw inside strings, so round 3's transcript reader (kept as it is) and the old stream readers dropped such a record; a take whose transcript carries one, or a non-blank line that is not JSON, fails closed. It routes by the generic operator-reason rows like harness-condition-violated: harness-error after the agent's first turn, a rehearsal before it. tests/test_routing.py TestRound4Additions binds it.
transcript-unreadable.meaning: the transcript cannot be read one JSON record per newline-split line: it carries a line separator other than newline (U+2028, U+2029, \x85, \r, \x0b, \x0c, \x1c-\x1e), or a non-blank line is not JSON

harness-condition-violated.ruling: glitch-6b's ruling, 15 Oct 2026, under Javier's delegation (Javier approved the bash-first steer off, "Your call sounds good"): every claude-code take runs with CLAUDE_CODE_THRIFTY_SONIC off, and (the isolation ruling, the same day) denies RemoteTrigger, SendMessage and ListAgents; a take where such a harness condition failed is routed as harness-error, since a harness condition failed, which is not the agent's behaviour. It routes by the generic operator-reason rows, harness-error after the agent's first turn (a rehearsal before it, as every operator reason). tests/test_routing.py TestRound4Additions binds it.
harness-condition-violated.meaning: a study harness condition did not hold for the take, fail closed on every turn (glitch-6b, 15 Oct 2026): a turn has no launch journal, or its journal does not set CLAUDE_CODE_THRIFTY_SONIC to "false", deny RemoteTrigger, SendMessage and ListAgents (--disallowedTools and permissions.deny) or set crossSessionInbound "refuse"; the transcript still carries an auto_mode attachment; or a turn's stream init still offers a denied isolation tool

no-first-agent-turn.meaning: the process exited, or the transcript holds no agent text, before the agent's first turn

readers-disagree.meaning: the transcript reader and the record reader count different numbers of user turns

unknown-harness-origin.meaning: a user record carries a harness origin this file does not name

no-session-id.meaning: the transcript records no session id

script-not-a-list.meaning: the half's operator script is not a list of turns

operator-lines.meaning: a scripted line was not sent, was sent twice or in the wrong order, a recovery exceeded its limit, or a line not on the script was sent

stop-at-held-marker.meaning: the driver stopped at a marker it read as unheld, and the agent's reply holds it

fixture-binding.meaning: the fixture the driver built is not the half's pinned fixture, or the record of it is unreadable

leak-in-operator-turn.meaning: an operator line contains a pre-registered leak word

leak-in-loaded-context.meaning: the session's loaded context contains a leak word outside a pinned excusal

inherited-context.meaning: the session was given an instruction file, a working directory or a connector tool from outside its checkout

project-name.meaning: no operator line names the neutral project name derived from the session id

session-binding.meaning: the transcript is not bound by its session id to a committed ledger row of this task and half

invocation.meaning: the checker was called with a ledger row for a walk, or without one for a take

model-binding.meaning: an assistant record carries a model other than the one the attempt is registered to

constant-binding.meaning: the take's ledger shows a turn budget or permission mode other than the pre-registered ones, or no ledger

continued-past-unheld-marker.meaning: an operator line was sent after a reply that did not hold the previous step's marker, or a recovery was sent where its own marker was not held

checkout-binding.meaning: the session's recorded git status or loaded instruction file is not the checkout the driver builds from the pinned tree

stop-without-a-wait-point.meaning: the ledger records a stop at a step that carries no wait point, or with a further operator line sent after it

outcome-binding.meaning: the ledger's outcome is not one the pinned driver writes, or a turn row carries no exit code, or the outcome disagrees with the driver's own record of the run: a completed take whose turn was cut or whose last reply stops short of the end of a turn, or a take published as cut with no cut behind it

environment-record.meaning: the attempt's environment record is absent or unreadable, or disagrees with the draft's vocabulary, its transcript's session, its row's commit, its ledger or its own turns

rehearsal.source: Key renamed from reruns_per_half_cell (glitch-f3, 6 Oct 2026): the value counts the half-cell's committed rehearsals, this one included, so it allows at most cap−1 re-runs. Plan: 're-run in the same slot (capped at 3 per half-cell, round 3's cap)'. Round 3's prereg.json sets rehearsal_cap = 3 (at e2979b3143081824aadea73523ec41af30c1ddb1), and takes.py:286-291 there applies it per cell (task, half, model): a cell that has had rehearsal_cap rehearsals registers no further attempt: 'It publishes `incomplete — mechanical` with each reason, and no further attempt is registered.' Unit (glitch-f3's ruling, in-plan, 6 Oct 2026; recorded as glitch-f3's, not the owner's): the cap counts the rehearsals committed in the half-cell, round 3's unit, round 3's cell (task, half, model) being round 4's half-cell (arm, task, half, model), the registered row's half_cell, with wording and repeat or pressure as the slot inside it. batch.py counts every committed rehearsal of the half-cell, one by one (a take a ruling routes rehearsal counts too: review round 3, W1B3-1); the one that brings the count to the cap is its slot's last (never re-run) and is committed with the cell state labels4.INCOMPLETE_MECHANICAL and its reason; nothing more is registered for that half-cell, and the loop goes on with the other half-cells. Each rehearsal's own reasons stay in its own committed record.

harness-error.beyond_cap: published as harness-error in its own column; leaves the denominator, the cell's n printed
harness-error.source: Plan: 'one re-run in the same slot (capped at 2 per half-cell)'.

pause.source: Key renamed from reruns_per_half_cell (glitch-f3, 6 Oct 2026): the value counts the half-cell's usage-window events of pause, the one that reaches it included, so at most cap−1 of them are re-run (W1B3-5, below). Plan: 're-run in the same slot under round 3's pause_cap'. Round 3's files say two things, both recorded here (review round 2, W1B2-11). Its driver, evals/gap-study-3/drive.py:147-148 at e2979b3143081824aadea73523ec41af30c1ddb1 (review 13, F6): 'a pause is uncapped where a rehearsal is capped, so a death before the first turn whose message merely says "resets" must not be read as a pause.' Its pre-registration nonetheless sets pause_cap = 3 (evals/gap-study-3/prereg.json), and evals/gap-study-3/takes.py:280-285 applies it per cell (task, half, model): 'A pause frees a slot on the driver's record alone, so it is capped like a rehearsal; the cell publishes `incomplete — mechanical` and no further attempt is registered.' The pre-registered value is the one round 3 enforced (takes.py reads pre['pause_cap']), and round 4 copies it, 3 per half-cell, under Javier's ruling "gap4 routing: A" (6 Oct 2026). Unit (glitch-f3's ruling, in-plan, 6 Oct 2026; recorded as glitch-f3's, not the owner's): the cap counts per half-cell, round 3's unit, round 3's cell (task, half, model) being round 4's half-cell (arm, task, half, model), the registered row's half_cell, with wording and repeat or pressure as the slot inside it. What it counts (glitch-f3's ruling on review round 3, W1B3-5, in-plan, 6 Oct 2026, relayed by the gap4 lane lead; recorded as glitch-f3's, not the owner's): the half-cell's usage-window events, so the pauses that share one reset count once. The cap bounds window events, round 3's own unit: round 3 drove one take at a time, so each of its pauses was its own window event, while round 4 drives up to three takes in a block and every pause of one block shares the one reset the loop waits for before its next block. Each committed pause carries its window_event, and batch.py counts the distinct window events among the half-cell's committed pauses (a take a ruling routes pause counts as its own event: review round 3, W1B3-1); the take whose window event brings the count to the cap is its slot's last (never re-run) and is committed with the cell state labels4.INCOMPLETE_MECHANICAL and its reason, as is every later take of that half-cell; nothing more is registered for it, and the loop goes on with the other half-cells (still waiting for the usage window before its next launch).

graded.source: Plan: 'no try is ever discarded or re-run for something the agent did'.

pin_refusal.source: Review round 3, W1B3-2: the gap4 lane lead's ruling, whose stricter reading glitch-f3 accepted (in-plan, 6 Oct 2026, relayed by the gap4 lane lead; recorded as glitch-f3's, not the owner's), carrying glitch-f3's fold-3 ruling 2, 'a differing init is refused for a human, a pin mismatch'. Before the agent's first turn, a take whose init events include one that is present and differs from the pin (its model, mode or version) is refused for a human, whatever else matches: no before-first-turn harness row (an API error, no-first-agent-turn, a container exit, a silent timeout) turns a pin mismatch into a rehearsal. Only a route in outranked_by wins over it, the rate-limit pause, because pause outranks every route and a usage limit is not a pin fault. A missing init event never triggers it (glitch-f3's fold-3 ruling: a CLI that never printed its init event is harness-side). After the first turn the init-mismatch row routes a differing or missing init as harness-error, as the plan says. Its scope is this one rule, on its all_of line: if glitch-f3 narrows it to timed-out ends only, that is one condition appended there, {"path": "ledger.end", "op": "eq", "value": "timed-out"}. routing.py checks the rule: before the first turn, conditions on harness records only, and only routes that outrank rehearsal may outrank it.

rows.source: Plan table row 1: 'before the agent's first turn | preflight failure'. Also a box-only record (CP1 task: 'the box-only records (preflight, ...)').
Plan table row 1: 'container start failure'. Lane w1b decision: a container that started and exited before the first turn counts as a start failure.

Plan table row 1: 'API error'. A rate-limit marker also matches rate-limit (pause), which wins on precedence. Phase per the gap4 lane lead's ruling on W1B-5: the agent's first turn starts with the first turn that produced completed agent output (a text or tool-call message, read from the stream's event types), so an API error in a turn that produced none, however that turn ended (in error, or timed out), is before the agent's first turn. Review round 2 (W1B2-1) reverted 3fcab58d, which had let any timed-out turn start the agent's turn and so sent this row's silent-timeout cases to harness-error; glitch-f3's correction (6 Oct 2026; glitch-f3's, not the owner's) keeps a silent timeout before the first turn (see silent-timeout-before-first-turn).

CP1 task: 'the box-only records (preflight, sidecar health, ...)'. Lane w1b decision: a watcher fault before the first turn is a rehearsal, as every other harness fault in that phase. The stop record is not read here: before the first turn it may legitimately not exist yet.
Plan table last row: 'each operator-side reason the copied checker keeps ... a rehearsal before the first turn'. Matches any id in operator_reasons (PENDING, see operator_reasons_status).

CP1 task: 'The sidecar's health and the operator-diff check run inside that same step'; CP3 endstate: 'The drive step has already routed any operator-step diff that no event explains'. Phase split as the plan's last row.

Plan table last row: 'round 3's finalize abort (drive.py:1417) ... a rehearsal before the first turn'. Round 3's own treatment, recorded beside the plan's re-route (review round 2, W1B2-11; evals/gap-study-3/drive.py:1405-1419 at e2979b3143081824aadea73523ec41af30c1ddb1): when stage 00's finalize did not write samples.csv within the wait, its driver set the ledger outcome to 'aborted — finalize did not write samples.csv within {wait_s} s' (line 1417) and sent nothing further, because 'the take has a first agent turn, so it is graded, and the label whose definition it meets is `aborted`' (lines 1408-1409). Round 4 routes the same record by phase, as the plan's table says: a rehearsal here, before the agent's first turn, and harness-error after it (finalize-abort-after-first-turn), never the graded aborted round 3 gave it.

glitch-f3's correction (6 Oct 2026, relayed by the gap4 lane lead; recorded as glitch-f3's, not the owner's), which withdrew his earlier acceptance that a timed-out silent first turn is the agent's: "A silent timeout with no completed agent output can't be told apart from a hung API, CLI or egress using harness records, and round 3 already routes it as rehearsal through no-first-agent-turn. 'A timeout stays the agent's' applies once the agent has produced completed output." Plan table row 1: before the agent's first turn, a harness fault is a rehearsal. This row's route is its one value in routing.json: a ruling change is a one-word edit of it. It sits at rehearsal's level, so every before-first-turn harness row it meets (an API error, an operator reason such as no-first-agent-turn, a container exit, a preflight failure) names the same route and is one answer with it, and the rate-limit row (pause) outranks it. Review round 2, W1B2-1 (the gap4 lane lead's brief): its own row, any_of ledger.end eq timed-out. glitch-f3's ruling (in-plan, 6 Oct 2026, relayed by the gap4 lane lead in lane w1b's third fold; recorded as glitch-f3's, not the owner's), as relayed: "A CLI that never printed its init event is harness-side, by the same reason as W1B2-1." So a silent timeout with no init event matches this row and rehearses. A silent timeout whose init event is present and names another model, mode or version is refused for a human (a pin mismatch), but not by this row: review round 3 (W1B3-2) found that a none_of here held only while no other before-first-turn row matched (a differing init plus no-first-agent-turn, an API 500 or a container exit still rehearsed), so the check moved to the table's one pin refusal (pin_refusal, init-differs-before-first-turn), which refuses it whatever else matches; glitch-f3 accepted that stricter reading (in-plan, 6 Oct 2026; glitch-f3's, not the owner's). The row is before-first-turn and the init-mismatch row after-first-turn, so the two never meet and cannot tie; after the first turn a missing init event stays a mismatch (differs_from_pin, lane w1b decision 5).

Plan table: 'any time | a pre-registered rate-limit marker in the API-error record | pause'. The markers are the take's own harness's (rate_limit_markers keyed by harness, read by the take's pin.harness: lane w4h-w1b-next-touch, item 1); a spend-cap marker is refused before this row is read (spend_cap_refusal). Every API error of the take is read (W1B-4): a marker on any one of them matches. A marker in any of the record's three fields matches: structured status or type, OR round 3's text markers in the harness-side error text, never the agent's (glitch-f3's ruling, 6 Oct 2026; see rate_limit_markers.source).
Plan table: 'after the first turn | the turn's out-of-memory or pids-limit counters rose ... whatever the exit looked like | aborted ... never re-run'.
Plan table: 'after the first turn | API-error record'.
Plan table: 'after the first turn | ... container exit'.
Plan table: 'a watcher gap (start or stop record missing, non-zero exit, queue overflow)'; edge case: 'The watcher overflows or dies mid-take: the take routes as harness-error'.

Plan table: 'an init event whose model, mode or version differs from the pin'; testing strategy: 'a mismatch on the last turn of an otherwise graded take is a harness-error'. Lane w1b decision: a turn with no init event at all counts as a mismatch, after the agent's first turn. Before it, a missing init event is harness-side (glitch-f3's ruling of 6 Oct 2026: a silent timeout with no init event rehearses, see silent-timeout-before-first-turn), and an init event that is present and differs from the pin is refused for a human whatever else matches (pin_refusal; review round 3, W1B3-2).

Plan table: 'after the first turn | a non-zero exec exit with no API-error record and no rise in those counters | harness-error'. Lane w1b decision: the exit of a turn the host ended as timed-out is not read, because 'a timeout stays the agent's' and the host's own kill exits non-zero.
Plan table last row: '... harness-error after it'. Matches any id in operator_reasons (PENDING, see operator_reasons_status).

annotations_about: Annotations are decided on every take, in every phase, whatever route wins and even when routing refuses the take: they never route. An annotation holds when at least one of its any_of conditions holds; it is reported as an event when event is true, and sets mask (the take's text is masked, never deleted, before commit) when mask is true.
